title_zh: 那句“这是你的职责”，从哪里来？
title_en: How Did This Become My Job?
deck_zh: 一份月底前要交的清单，一句“以前一直这样”，一个并不赞同却仍在其中的岗位。先别急着问自己够不够负责，先问这件事怎样落到了自己身上。
deck_en: A handover due on Friday, a manager saying “we have always done it this way,” a role you occupy without endorsing everything it asks. Before asking whether you are responsible enough, ask how this became yours to answer for.
body_zh: 设想你刚接手一个部门。桌上有电脑、钥匙，还有一份月底前必须交出的清单。你问清单是谁定的，前任说，一直这样。你问其中两项为什么也归你，他有点惊讶：你现在不是坐在这个位置上吗？
这句话听起来足够结束谈话。你也可能马上开始反省，是不是自己太计较，别人交代一件事，何必追问这么多。但你问的还不是要不要认真做，而是另一件更早的事：这项要求究竟怎样成了你的职责？
事情确实可以落在你身上，却并不是因为有人用了一个很重的词。也不是你一进门，前任留下的、同事希望的、公司想要的，就都自动变成同一种东西。把它们分清，不是为了少做一点，而是免得最后连自己在承担什么都不知道。
## 不是所有期待，都是职责
同事希望你顺便替她整理旧资料。她很忙，你也有能力帮忙，这些都是真的。但能力、需要和期待，还不足以单独回答：她是否有根据要求你做？你的岗位确实接下了这项事吗？要求做到什么程度，什么时候算完成？
另一项交接却不同。你这次任职已经明确接下月底前核对库存的工作，谁向你提出要求、清单包括什么、出现争议怎样追问，也都能找到。不只是别人盼着你做，而是一项可以说明来路的要求，实际落在了你这一次任职里。你可以不同意它的安排，仍得承认，它不是凭空想象出来的。
后面会把这一步叫作‘登记’。不是说一定填过一张表，更不是只要表上写了名字就算数；它说的是，某项要求实际进入了这个人在这段关系中的行动处境。一个表格可能只是记录，也可能写着不曾真正生效的东西。重要的仍是要求怎样实际落地。
这里先作一个小小的区别：要求已经落到身上，和要求的内容值得赞同，不是一回事。登记也不必事事出于本人自愿，不能只凭不赞同，就断定关系没有实际成立。你觉得一个流程笨，未必就说明流程从未适用于你；一项流程确实适用于你，也不能证明它一点问题没有。若只有‘我愿意’和‘什么都没有’两个格子，许多真实的处境便无处可放。
判断也不能停在纸上。岗位手册可能印着一条始终没有施用于这次任职的旧规定；一个组织也可能只留下漂亮的制度名称，实际上从没有相应的承认、程序和支持。反过来，平时没有人处罚，并不足以证明一项要求没有运行。要看的是实际关系，不是纸张有多正式，也不是上司最近有没有发过脾气。
更不能把威胁全叫作职责。绑匪也会提出清楚的要求，也能使人不得不改变行动；这不因此成为人质的岗位责任。本文讨论的是有相应权利位置、实际支持与登记关系的社会要求，不是把每一道能逼人服从的命令，都换成一个体面的名字。
这一区别不会神奇地使强迫消失。说清一句命令没有这样的来源，并不表示受威胁的人立刻就安全了。它只是阻止我们再添上一层混淆：已经在受压迫，还被说成是没有尽责。概念帮我们看清发生了什么，保护仍要靠现实里的通道和安排。
## 一个岗位，不是一只装旧账的箱子
再看‘你坐在这个位置上’。这句话可能指财务主管这个职能，可能指眼前的你，也可能指你在这家公司里的这一次任职。三件事看着挨得很近，却不能互相代替。岗位可以一直存在，人可以换；同一个人离开多年再回来，也可以是另一段任职。
这是为什么，前任漏报的一笔，不会仅仅因为你坐上了他的椅子，就变成你当年漏报的。历史不能这样换人。但公司现在是否另外交给你一项核查旧账的工作，又是另一个问题。旧事可以成为新要求的内容，不能因为它说的是旧事，就预先断言它一定有来源，或一定没有来源。
相反的偷换也要防着。公司换了名字、换了股东，甚至搬了办公室，不能只看招牌就说一切从头开始。原来那次任职和其中的安排是否续行，仍得看实际发生了什么。承担的实例与支撑它的载体有关，却不是每换一个外壳，原有任职就自动结束。
同一次任职里，也可以有几项走法不同的要求。核对清单是一项，到期交完便完成；持续照管某份资料是另一项，怎样完成、何时结束，要看那一项自己的内容。不能因为其中一件做完了，就说整个岗位从此没有任何事；也不能因为岗位还在，就让已经完成的要求永远悬着。
所以，追问来路不是一句聪明的拒绝话术。它有时会发现，你被塞进了一项没有根据的要求；有时会发现，眼前的安排确实已把某件事交给了你。它不预先保证让你轻松，只是要求每一笔都说得出来：由谁、凭什么、在什么关系里、要这个人做什么。
## 要求在身上，不等于事情已经做了
公司提出核对库存，是要求发出的那一头；这项要求实际落在你的任职里，是你承接的那一头；你后来把清单交出来，才是兑现。后两件都在你这一侧，却不是同一件事。手里有一项待完成的要求，和已经完成它，差着一次真实的行动。
这个区别在做完时不显眼，没做完时就显出来。月底到了，清单没交，不能说既然动作没有发生，就什么也不存在了。正因为有一项先已成立的要求，我们才有可能问：它为什么落空？但推论不能倒过来。有人失望，不能单凭失望证明，你本来就欠他这一项。
兑现也不总是一个看得见的动作。某项关于资料的要求，可能恰恰由不把它说出去来兑现。相反，提出要求本身也可以是一个动作。我们分的是同一件事从提出、落地到兑现的不同状态，不是在规定只有忙起来、交出东西才算行动。
现在，你可以把桌上那份清单摊开，不先替自己判懒惰，也不先替全部要求盖章。有一项确实属于这次任职，但时间安排需要重谈；有一项只是同事的期待，你愿不愿意帮忙，可以另说；还有一项涉及前任的错误，需要区分当年的过失与现在的核查。三个问题不再挤成一句‘这是你的职责’。
接下来的讨论才可能具体。你没有靠一个词把工作推开，也没有把整个自己交给一个岗位。你只是先弄清：这一次，到底是哪一项事，怎样找到了你。
body_en: Imagine taking over a small department. On the desk are a laptop, a set of keys, and a list that must be completed before the end of the month. You ask who decided what belongs on it. Your predecessor says it has always been this way. You ask why two particular items belong to you. He seems surprised: aren't you the person in this position now?

That sounds like the end of the conversation. You may even begin apologizing for being difficult. Yet you have not asked whether the work deserves care. You have asked an earlier question: how did this particular demand become yours to answer for? Being conscientious cannot settle the question of what you have undertaken.

Several things may have accumulated on the same desk: unfinished work, reasonable hopes, favors, instructions, and obligations attached to this appointment. Their proximity does not make them identical. Separating them is not necessarily a way to do less. It is a way to know what you are doing.
## An expectation needs more than disappointment

A colleague hopes you will reorganize an old archive. She needs help and you know how to provide it. Neither fact alone establishes that this is work she can require from you. What arrangement places it within your appointment? What does it include, and what would count as completing it? A genuine need can matter without answering all those questions.

The inventory handover is different. In this imagined arrangement, your appointment specifically includes checking the stock before the month closes. The scope, the person entitled to direct the work, and the means of questioning an instruction can be identified. This is not merely someone's wish. An identifiable demand has become operative in this particular appointment.

The paper calls this becoming operative registration. It need not mean filling in a form, and a name on a form is not sufficient. It concerns a demand actually entering this person's situation within the relationship. A document can record that event, or describe something that never became effective. The document and the operative relation are not identical.

You may dislike the arrangement. That does not, by itself, make the demand imaginary. Registration need not be voluntary in every instance; personal disagreement alone cannot establish that no operative relation exists. Nor does the fact that a demand is operative establish that its content deserves approval. We need room to describe a requirement we really face without pretending that it has become our own conviction. The alternatives cannot be limited to wholehearted endorsement or complete nonexistence.

Paperwork alone will not settle this either. A handbook may contain a provision never applied to your appointment. A formally named institution may lack the recognition, procedures, or actual support needed for its demands to operate in the relevant way. But the absence of a recent punishment proves little on its own. An arrangement can remain effective without somebody exercising every available sanction. The question concerns the actual relationship, not how official the paper looks or how angry a manager sounds.

There is also a boundary before this inquiry begins. A kidnapper can issue a clear instruction and force someone to change course. That does not turn the instruction into the hostage's job. The account here concerns demands grounded in functioning rights positions and the relations through which they operate. Bare force does not acquire that standing simply by being effective.

Distinguishing force from accountability does not make a threatened person safe. A better description is not a rescue mechanism. It does prevent an additional mistake: describing someone already under coercion as merely failing to do their duty. Practical protection still requires arrangements that work outside the sentence.
## The chair does not inherit every unfinished story

Being ‘the person in this position’ can mean three different things. There is the organizational function, there is the individual, and there is that individual's particular appointment within the function. A position can outlast its holder. One person can leave and return years later. Neither the continuing title nor the familiar name makes every appointment the same event.

Your predecessor's failure to report a transaction does not become your historical act because you occupy the same chair. But that is distinct from whether you have now been assigned to investigate the old accounts. An earlier event may supply the subject matter of a new demand. Its age alone proves neither that the new demand has a source nor that it cannot have one.

The reverse shortcut is no better. A changed company name, a new owner, or a different office does not automatically end every existing arrangement. We have to ask whether the appointment and its operative relations continue. Changing a carrier is not necessarily changing the instance of accountability it supports.

Several demands can also coexist within one appointment. The inventory is a one-time deliverable. Another requirement concerning the handling of information may continue under its own specified conditions. Finishing the first does not complete the second. Keeping the position does not make a finished deliverable permanently unfinished either. Each demand needs enough particularity to have a life of its own.

Tracing a source is therefore not a clever synonym for refusing. It may reveal an unsupported instruction. It may also establish that a piece of work really has been assigned. The inquiry offers no advance guarantee that you will like the result. It asks each demand to identify who issues it, through which authority and arrangement, to whom, and with what content.
## Carrying a demand is not yet carrying it out

The company issues the inventory requirement. It becomes operative in your appointment. You later perform the handover. These are three states along one route, not three unrelated demands. The last two are on your side: carrying something that calls for an answer, and actually answering it.

When the work is done, the distinction may seem unnecessary. When it is missed, it matters. The deadline passes without a completed list. The act has not occurred, yet something can still be identified as unfulfilled. That is possible because the requirement was distinct from its performance. But the reasoning runs only one way. Someone's disappointment cannot establish that an applicable requirement existed in the first place.

Performance need not be conspicuous activity. A requirement to keep certain information confidential may be met by not disclosing it. Issuing an instruction can itself be an act. The distinction is between a demand, its becoming operative for a bearer, and its fulfillment—not between people who visibly do something and people who seem still.

The list can now be spread across the desk without becoming a verdict on your character. One item belongs to your appointment but needs a more workable deadline. Another is a colleague's hope; helping can be discussed without pretending it was already assigned. A third requires separating an old failure from the present task of investigating it.

Those are three different conversations. They were hidden inside one phrase: your responsibility. You have neither escaped the work by changing its name nor handed your whole person over to the job. You have begun with a smaller question that makes the others possible: what, this time, has actually reached you?
